introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0565 Human Biology 1, June 2023, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; select only one answer. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one best answer, A, B, C or D. Questions 23 to 26 use the 1, 2, 3 combinations (A: 1, 2 and 3 correct; B: 1 and 2 only; C: 2 and 3 only; D: 1 only).

figures.legende: Median section of the brain with four numbered parts: 1 cerebrum, 2 cerebellum, 3 lower brain stem (medulla region), 4 region of the hypothalamus and pituitary (Question 10).
Graph of rate of reaction against temperature (0 to 60 degrees C) with four points marked: I low rate, II rising part, III peak, IV falling part (Question 15).
Human female reproductive system with four labelled parts I to IV: I top of the uterus, II oviduct, III cervix region, IV lower end near the vagina (Question 32).
Nitrogen cycle boxes (atmosphere, nitrates, ammonium compounds, plant proteins, animal proteins) with arrows numbered 1 to 4 (Question 42).

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the feature that makes man structurally different from other mammals.
questions.corrige_markdown: External ears, heterodont teeth (incisors, canines, premolars, molars) and a four-chambered heart are found in nearly all mammals, so they do not set man apart. Man has a fully opposable thumb that can touch each finger tip, giving a precise grip; most other mammals lack it. Option D is the only one that separates man from mammals in general. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Two solutions separated by a permeable membrane with equal movement of water in both directions are described as being:
questions.corrige_markdown: Equal movement of water in both directions means there is no net movement, so the two solutions have the same water potential (same solute concentration). Solutions with equal concentration are isotonic. Hypertonic and hypotonic describe a solution that is more or less concentrated than another. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which cell organelle synthesizes proteins?
questions.corrige_markdown: Proteins are assembled on ribosomes (on free ribosomes or on the rough endoplasmic reticulum). The nucleus holds the genetic instructions, the mitochondrion releases energy and the lysosome digests materials. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the tissues bind organs together in the body?
questions.corrige_markdown: Connective tissue (for example areolar tissue, tendons and ligaments) supports and binds organs together. Epithelial tissue covers and lines surfaces, nervous tissue conducts impulses, and skeletal tissue (bone, cartilage) supports the body. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Meiosis is a type of cell division that occurs in:
questions.corrige_markdown: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and occurs in the reproductive organs (testes and ovaries) to form gametes, the sex cells. Somatic cells, body cells and muscle cells divide by mitosis. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Soaking a piece of mammalian limb bone into dilute HCl for a few hours makes it:
questions.corrige_markdown: Dilute hydrochloric acid dissolves the calcium salts that make bone hard. What remains is mainly the organic collagen fibres, so the bone becomes soft and flexible (it can even be tied in a knot). Brittleness comes from the mineral salts, which have been removed (a bone that is heated instead becomes brittle). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the characteristics which best describes skeletal muscle:
questions.corrige_markdown: Skeletal (striated, voluntary) muscle has long cylindrical fibres with many nuclei; it contracts quickly but fatigues easily. Never tiring is a feature of cardiac muscle, which has branched, uninucleated fibres. Spindle-shaped fibres belong to smooth muscle. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Has elongated and multinucleated fibres which contract fast and easily get tired.
Has elongated and multinucleated fibres which contract fast and never get tired
Has spindle shaped and multinucleated fibres which contract fast and never get tired.
Has branched and uninucleated fibres which contract fast and never get tired

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the structure which prevents dislocation of bones during movement.
questions.corrige_markdown: Ligaments are tough, slightly elastic bands that join bone to bone across a joint and hold the bones in position, so they prevent dislocation. Cartilage cushions the bone ends, tendons join muscle to bone and synovial fluid lubricates the joint. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is the direction of transmission of a nerve impulse along a neuron?
questions.corrige_markdown: In a neurone the impulse enters through the dendrites, travels along the dendron to the cell body and then leaves along the axon towards the axon terminals. Option B is the only sequence that starts at the dendrite and ends at the axon. Option D has the printed misspelling 'dentrite' and a wrong order. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
![fig-1](gce-ol-human-biology-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

Which of the part indicated on the diagram of the brain below controls the breathing rate?
questions.corrige_markdown: The breathing rate is controlled by the breathing centre in the medulla oblongata, the lowest part of the brain that joins the spinal cord (part 3). Part 1 is the cerebrum (thinking, memory), part 2 is the cerebellum (balance and coordination) and part 4 is the hypothalamus/pituitary region (temperature and hormones). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the eye defect that can be corrected using a concave lens.
questions.corrige_markdown: In myopia (short sight) the eyeball is too long or the lens too strong, so light from distant objects focuses in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens spreads the rays first and moves the image back onto the retina. Hypermetropia and presbyopia need a convex lens, and astigmatism a cylindrical lens. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the gland which secretes both hormones and enzymes in the human body.
questions.corrige_markdown: The pancreas is a mixed gland: its islets of Langerhans secrete insulin and glucagon (hormones) into the blood, while its other cells secrete pancreatic juice with digestive enzymes (amylase, trypsin, lipase) into the duodenum. The pituitary, thyroid and adrenal glands secrete hormones only. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How does adrenaline affects the heart beat rate and the functioning of the liver?
questions.corrige_markdown: Adrenaline prepares the body for fight or flight: it raises the heart rate and stimulates the liver to convert stored glycogen into glucose, which raises the blood sugar for respiration in the muscles. Converting glucose to glycogen is the effect of insulin. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Causes heart beat to decrease and liver to convert glucose to glycogen
Causes heart  beat to decrease and liver to convert glycogen to glucose
Causes heart  beat to increase and liver convert glycogen  to glucose
Causes the heart  beat to increase and liver convert  glucose to glycogen

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose a mineral element necessary in the diet for the prevention of goiter.
questions.corrige_markdown: The thyroid gland needs iodine to make thyroxine. A lack of iodine makes the gland swell, a condition called goiter. Iron prevents anaemia, calcium builds bones and teeth. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The graph below shows the effect of temperature on an enzyme controlled reaction.

![fig-2](gce-ol-human-biology-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

Which one of the points corresponds to the optimum temperature for this reaction?
questions.corrige_markdown: The optimum temperature is the temperature at which the rate of reaction is highest, that is the top of the curve, point III. Point II is on the rising part (the rate is still increasing) and point IV is on the falling part where the enzyme is being denatured. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A digestive disorder characterized by the sending out of hard faeces is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Constipation means that faeces stay too long in the large intestine, too much water is absorbed and the faeces become hard and difficult to pass. Diarrhoea gives watery faeces, dysentery gives bloody diarrhoea with an infection, and gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select a disaccharide below which when hydrolyzed produces only glucose molecules.
questions.corrige_markdown: Maltose is glucose + glucose. Lactose gives glucose + galactose and sucrose gives glucose + fructose. Starch is a polysaccharide, not a disaccharide, so it is excluded even though it gives only glucose. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the statements below is true of inspiration.
questions.corrige_markdown: During inspiration the diaphragm muscles contract and the diaphragm flattens, which increases the volume of the chest cavity and lowers the pressure, so air enters the lungs. Relaxation with a dome shape happens in expiration. A contracting diaphragm cannot be dome-shaped (B) and a relaxed one cannot flatten (C). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Diaphragm muscles  contract giving the diaphragm a flattened shape
Diaphragm muscles  contract giving  the diaphragm a dome shape
Diaphragm muscles relax and the diaphragm flattens.
Diaphragm muscles relax and become dome-shaped.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a short- term effect of exercise on the breathing rate.
questions.corrige_markdown: During exercise the muscles respire faster and produce more carbon dioxide. The rise in blood carbon dioxide stimulates the breathing centre, so the breathing rate increases at once. Larger diaphragm muscles and a larger lung volume are long-term training effects. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Increase in the volume of the lungs

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following blood vessels is superficially located in the body?
questions.corrige_markdown: Veins lie near the surface of the body (the veins on the back of the hand can be seen), whereas arteries are deep in the tissues where their thick, pulsating walls are protected. Capillaries and arterioles are microscopic vessels inside the tissues. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How is Lymph different from blood?
questions.corrige_markdown: Lymph flows in one direction only, from the tissues towards the veins near the heart, and valves in the lymph vessels prevent backflow. Blood circulates in a closed loop. Lymph moves by body muscle contraction, not by the heart (A), has no platelets (C) and does not contain more nutrients than blood (D). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Movement of Lymph is by the pumping action  of the heart
Lymph flows in one direction only
Lymph contains more digestive food nutrients

questions.enonce_markdown: Anaemia is a blood disorder caused by:
questions.corrige_markdown: Anaemia is a shortage of red blood cells or of haemoglobin, so the blood carries too little oxygen and the person feels weak and tired. Lack of white cells reduces immunity, lack of platelets affects clotting. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 23 to 26: one or more of the responses is (are) correct. Choose: A if 1, 2 and 3 are correct; B if 1 and 2 only are correct; C if 2 and 3 only are correct; D if 1 only is correct.*

Are the homeostatic organs in the human body

1. Kidneys and Liver
2. Lungs and skin
3. Skin and kidneys
questions.corrige_markdown: Homeostasis keeps the internal environment constant. 1 is correct: the kidneys control water and salts and remove urea, and the liver regulates blood glucose and makes urea. 2 is correct: the lungs remove carbon dioxide and the skin controls body temperature. 3 is correct: skin and kidneys both regulate temperature, water and salts. All three pairs are homeostatic organs. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
How is vasodilation in the skin brought about?

1- Skin arterioles narrow and blood flow to the surface
2 - Skin arterioles dilate
3- Shunt vessels dilate

*Options as printed:* A) If 1, 2 and 3 are correct   B) If 1 and 2 only are correct   C) If 2 and 3 only are correct   D) If 1 only is correct
questions.corrige_markdown: Vasodilation in the skin happens when the body is too warm: the skin arterioles widen (statement 2 is true), more blood flows through the capillaries near the surface and heat is lost. Statement 1 is false (narrowing is vasoconstriction). Statement 3 is also false in the usual textbook account: the shunt vessels constrict during vasodilation, and they dilate when the body is cold (vasoconstriction) to bypass the surface capillaries. The strictly correct choice, '2 only', is not offered among the printed options, so the key is uncertain (the examiners probably meant C, 2 and 3 only). This question is left open for self-assessment. **Most likely expected answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 23 to 26: one or more of the responses is (are) correct. Choose: A if 1, 2 and 3 are correct; B if 1 and 2 only are correct; C if 2 and 3 only are correct; D if 1 only is correct.*

The part of the nephron which serves as the target for the action of Antidiuretic hormone:

1. Distal convoluted tubule
2. Glomerulus
3. Loop of Henle.
questions.corrige_markdown: ADH makes the walls of the distal convoluted tubule (and the collecting duct) more permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed. Statement 1 is true. The glomerulus only filters blood (2 false) and the loop of Henle builds the concentration gradient without being the target of ADH (3 false). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Questions 23 to 26: one or more of the responses is (are) correct. Choose: A if 1, 2 and 3 are correct; B if 1 and 2 only are correct; C if 2 and 3 only are correct; D if 1 only is correct.*

What usually happens after profuse sweating during exercise?

1. Less urine is formed
2. Blood becomes less concentrated
3. Less water is reabsorbed by the kidney
questions.corrige_markdown: Sweating removes water, so the blood becomes more concentrated (2 false). The pituitary gland releases more ADH, so the kidney reabsorbs more water (3 false) and a small volume of concentrated urine is formed (1 true). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a substance produced by the liver
questions.corrige_markdown: The liver makes bile, which is stored in the gall bladder and emulsifies fats. Insulin comes from the pancreas, glucose is absorbed from digested food (the liver only stores or releases it) and the liver does not make digestive enzymes. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A chemical barrier against pathogens that is provided by the eye is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Tears contain lysozyme, an enzyme that breaks down the cell walls of bacteria, so lysozyme is the chemical barrier. Tears alone mostly wash the eye mechanically, aqueous and vitreous humours keep the shape of the eye, and antibodies are part of the immune response, not a barrier. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The production of aqueous and vitreous humours

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose the correct sequence of events for a blood clot to be formed on a damaged tissue:
questions.corrige_markdown: When tissue is damaged, platelets break up and release thrombokinase (thromboplastin). With calcium ions it converts prothrombin to thrombin; thrombin converts soluble fibrinogen to insoluble fibrin, and the fibrin threads form a mesh that traps blood cells to make the clot. Option C gives these steps in the right order. A puts exposure of platelets last, B puts fibrinogen before thrombin and D omits fibrinogen/fibrin. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Release of thrombokinase, conversion of prothrombin to thrombin, formation of a mesh network, exposure of platelets to air.
Release  of thrombokinase, exposure of platelets to air, conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin , calcium ions convert prothrombin to  thrombin
Release of thrombokinase, conversion of prothrombin to thrombin, conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin, formation of a mesh network.
Release of  thrombokinase, calcium ions convert prothrombin to thrombin, exposure of platelets to air  formation of a mesh network

questions.enonce_markdown: A person with anti-A antibodies and anti-B antibodies in its plasma belongs to what blood group?
questions.corrige_markdown: A person makes antibodies against the antigens that he does not have. Anti-A and anti-B in the plasma mean that there are no A or B antigens on the red cells, so the person is group O. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which information about the male gamete is correct?
questions.corrige_markdown: The male gamete (sperm) is small and motile, with a tail, and millions are produced. The female gamete (ovum) is large, cannot move and usually only one is released at a time. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The male gamete is large in size  and cannot move
The male gamete is small in size and only one is produced at a time
The male gamete is large in size and many are produced.
The male gamete is small in size and many are produced.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below shows the reproductive structure of the human female.

![fig-3](gce-ol-human-biology-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

In which part does fertilization occur?
questions.corrige_markdown: Fertilization takes place in the upper part of the oviduct (Fallopian tube), part II, where the sperm meet the ovum shortly after ovulation. Part I is the uterus, where the embryo implants, part III is the cervix and part IV is the vagina. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the term often used to describe the continuous presence of malaria in a community.
questions.corrige_markdown: A disease that is always present in a community is endemic (malaria in many tropical areas). An epidemic is a sudden outbreak in a region, a pandemic spreads across several countries or continents, and sporadic means occasional isolated cases. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What main event characterizes the menstrual cycle in a human female?
questions.corrige_markdown: If the ovum is not fertilized, the thick uterine lining breaks down and is shed with blood and the unfertilized egg through the vagina; this is menstruation. The other options describe semen, poorly formed eggs or haemorrhage, which are not part of the cycle. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The release of blood and accumulated semen
The release of blood and poorly formed eggs
Break down of uterine lining and its release with unfertilized egg

questions.enonce_markdown: What are the possible genotypes of offspring resulting from the marriage between a male of blood group O and a female of blood group AB?
questions.corrige_markdown: Male group O is $ii$ (OO), so every gamete carries O. Female group AB is $I^AI^B$ and gives A or B. Offspring are therefore AO (group A) and BO (group B), and no child can be OO or AB. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: During the birth process, what initiates the rhythmic contractions of the walls of the uterus?
questions.corrige_markdown: The pituitary gland releases oxytocin, which stimulates the uterine muscle to contract rhythmically. The breaking of the amnion follows the start of labour, and the mother's push is voluntary and comes later. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The breakage of the amniotic Sac.
The head of the baby lying above the cervix
The release of the hormone Oxytocin
The voluntary push by the mother

questions.enonce_markdown: For a normal couple to have a colour blind Son, the woman's genotype must be;
questions.corrige_markdown: Colour blindness is sex-linked and recessive. A son gets his only X chromosome from his mother, so she must carry the allele $X^n$. As she is normal, she must be a carrier, $X^NX^n$. $X^nY$ and $X^NY$ are male genotypes, and $X^NX^N$ cannot give an affected son. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An organism having a pair of identical alleles is described as being
questions.corrige_markdown: Two identical alleles of a gene (AA or aa) make the organism homozygous for that gene. Heterozygous means two different alleles; homogametic and heterogametic refer to the sex chromosomes (XX and XY). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given the food chain below:
Grass→Chick → Snake→Hawk
What is the trophic level of the hawk?
questions.corrige_markdown: Grass is the producer, the chick is the primary consumer, the snake is the secondary consumer and the hawk is the tertiary consumer. The trap is to count the hawk as the fourth consumer because it is in the fourth position of the chain. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following diseases is caused by a virus ?
questions.corrige_markdown: Chicken pox is caused by the varicella-zoster virus. Cholera and diphtheria are bacterial diseases and candidiasis is a fungal infection. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the main component of the cell wall of Fungi.
questions.corrige_markdown: The cell walls of fungi are made mainly of chitin. Cellulose is the main component of the cell wall of plants, phospholipids make up cell membranes and glycogen is a storage carbohydrate. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the illustration of the nitrogen cycle below and answer the question that follows:

![fig-4](gce-ol-human-biology-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

What is the name of the bacterium that brings about the process numbered 2?
questions.corrige_markdown: Process 2 takes nitrogen from the atmosphere into the nitrogen of plant proteins. The conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into nitrogen compounds that plants use is nitrogen fixation, carried out by nitrogen-fixing bacteria (for example Rhizobium in root nodules, Azotobacter in the soil). Denitrifying bacteria return nitrogen to the air, nitrifying bacteria change ammonium compounds to nitrates, and putrefying bacteria change dead proteins to ammonium compounds. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is eutrophication?
questions.corrige_markdown: Eutrophication is the over-enrichment of a water body with nutrients (nitrates and phosphates). Algal overgrowth (B) is a result of it, while leaching of fertilizers (C) and sewage (D) are causes. Option A defines the process itself. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Over enrichment of a water body with excess nutrients
Overgrowth in the water body of algae and bacteria
Leaching of inorganic fertilizers from farmlands into a water body
The release of sewage effluent into a water body

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the principle of smoking as a method of food preservation ?
questions.corrige_markdown: Smoking dries the food: the heat and smoke remove water, and microbes cannot grow without water. The smoke also leaves some chemicals that slow their growth. Rapid heating then cooling describes pasteurisation (A), and smoking does not make food acidic (D). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The food is subjected to a high temperature and then rapidly cooled
Removes water from the food making it unfavourable for the growth of microbes
It denatures the natural enzymes  of the micro-organisms
Provides acid conditions that inhibit the growth of micro- organisms.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a common practice amongst students in a boarding school which should be discouraged.
questions.corrige_markdown: Sharing underwear and sportswear spreads skin infections, lice and fungal diseases, so it must be discouraged. Regular exercise and baths are good practice, and sharing meals is normal in a boarding school. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What causes smoker's cough?
questions.corrige_markdown: Cigarette smoke irritates the air passages and paralyses and destroys the cilia, so extra mucus builds up in the trachea and bronchi; the smoker coughs to clear it. Breakdown of alveolar walls is emphysema (B). Tar, not nicotine, is the main substance that damages the lining (D), and tar and mucus are not found 'inside' the lungs in the way option C describes. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The buildup of extra mucus in the trachea and bronchi
The breakdown of the walls of the lung alveolus
The buildup of extra mucus and tar inside the lungs
Nicotine that damages the lining of the trachea bronchi and bronchioles.

questions.enonce_markdown: Regular exercise is needed in the body to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Regular exercise strengthens the muscles and keeps them firm, which is good muscle tone, and it also helps the heart and lungs. Popularity and income are social side effects, not biological needs. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Burn up glucose and provoke hunger
Make the athlete a popular figure

questions.enonce_markdown: What kind of clinic should a mother with a new born baby attend?
questions.corrige_markdown: Postnatal care is for the mother and the baby after birth (check-ups, immunisation, feeding advice). Antenatal and prenatal care are the same thing and are given during pregnancy. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify one important role of play grounds from the list below.
questions.corrige_markdown: Playgrounds are sites for recreation and leisure, where people exercise and relax, which helps their physical and mental health. The other options are misuses of such places. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Hide out for thieves and delinquents
Help people to run away from problems.

questions.enonce_markdown: What first aid measure would you use when trying to rescue a person who has been electrocuted?
questions.corrige_markdown: The first step is to switch off the source of power so that the rescuer is not electrocuted and the victim stops receiving current. Only then can first aid and transport to hospital follow. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Rush victim to the hospital immediately
Switch off the source of power immediately
Administer first aid drugs to the victim.
Immobilize the part of the body affected.
